Being flagged under the national authority of the U.S., the primary applicable regulations are: o Code of Federal Regulations Title 46. Shipping o Code of Federal Regulations Title 33. Navigation and Navigable Waters After an extensive review of international and U.S. national regulations, the international application frame was reduced to a few IMO conventions. The applicability was transferred to U.S. national regulations. Most of the discarded conventions come from the characteristic Gross tonnage of MTV (280 GT), with the lower limit of applicability from most of the conventions being 500 GT. Another characteristic that removes the applicability of international regulation is that MTV is not going to perform international voyages. 1 Maltese Cross assigned to vessels and offshore units for which the hull construction and/or the manufacture of its machinery and components and any associated required testing, as applicable, is carried out under ABS survey. 2 Class Notation with Maltese Cross indicates compliance with the Hull requirements of the ABS Rules or their equivalent for unrestricted ocean service and survey by ABS during construction of the vessel. 3 This notation is assigned to barges designed and built in accordance with ABS Rules for Building and Classing Steel Barges *Only applied as GT reference for calculations and design requirements. Final Technical Report 19/57 3.3.1 Approval in Principle by ABS During the development of this project phase, it was convenient to involve ABS to reduce any risk regarding compliance with applicable standards in the remaining project stages. After discussing the project's current state, they suggested developing an Approval in Principle (AiP), which consisted of the revision of the General arrangement and the Midship section of the vessel. ABS proposed the regulation framework for the MTV as Shipping for Cargo and miscellaneous vessels. (CFR Title 46. Chapter I . Subchapter I). The final decision on applying this regulatory framework to the MTV belongs to the USCG; however, a few comments were raised and closed, followed by several actions taken. As a result, an AiP for the MTV was obtained from ABS. 3.3.2 Design Basis Agreement (USCG) When discussing project details with ABS, submission of a Design Basis Agreement (DBA) to the USCG was recommended due to the project's novelty, where several aspects must be directly determined. ABS supported IDOM in the preparation of this DBA. As of the publication of this report, a determination from the USCG is pending. Final Technical Report 20/57 4 STRUCTURAL DESIGN The structure design has been completed reevaluating the hull, completing the structure with several additional required elements and integrating the jack up towers.
